scope_note: Selected major wildfire disasters and fire seasons reported during the past decade. This is not a complete list of every wildfire: satellite detections do not map one-to-one to incidents, and no single global source provides a complete, consistently verified incident and casualty census.
death_method_note: Direct deaths are shown separately from estimated smoke-related mortality. A blank or ‘not reported’ responder count means the cited sources do not give a reliable breakdown; it does not mean zero.
location_note: Markers show approximate affected areas, not ignition points, fire perimeters, or exact casualty locations.

events.name: Los Angeles area fires
events.summary: The Palisades and Eaton fires destroyed neighborhoods across Los Angeles County. Official direct-death counts exclude modeled estimates of additional smoke-related deaths.

direct.label: 31 reported
direct.detail: Direct deaths attributed to the fires in the cited AP report.

responders.label: Not separately reported
responders.detail: The linked coverage does not provide a confirmed responder death total.

smoke.label: ≈440 estimated
smoke.detail: A separate study estimated excess deaths during the fire period; this is modeled smoke and health impact, not an official direct-fire toll.

sources.label: One-year report: fires killed at least 31 people
Report on estimated excess deaths linked to wildfire smoke

events.name: Southeastern Korea fires
events.summary: A fast-moving outbreak of fires across southeastern South Korea became the country’s worst recorded wildfire disaster. Reports identify firefighters and other response personnel among those killed.

direct.label: 31 reported
direct.detail: Latest direct-death toll reported in the linked AP coverage.

responders.label: At least 5 reported
responders.detail: AP reported a helicopter pilot and four firefighters/other response workers among those killed; classifications vary across reports.

sources.label: Follow-up reports 31 deaths, including a firefighting pilot
Wildfires killed 30; response workers among the dead

events.name: Valparaíso region fires
events.place: Viña del Mar and Valparaíso, Chile
events.summary: Fires swept through densely settled areas in central Chile. Investigators later charged a volunteer firefighter and a former forestry official in connection with starting the blaze; those accusations are not a finding about all causes.

direct.label: 137 reported
direct.detail: Deaths attributed to the Valparaíso region fires in the cited AP report.

responders.label: Not separately reported
responders.detail: The cited report does not establish a separate responder fatality count.

sources.label: Investigation into the fires that killed 137 people

events.name: Lahaina wildfire
events.summary: A wind-driven fire destroyed much of Lahaina. The final official toll is distinct from later research estimates of indirect effects such as smoke exposure.

direct.label: 102 reported
direct.detail: Maui Police Department identified 102 people who died.

responders.label: Not separately reported
responders.detail: The cited reporting does not provide a verified responder death count.

sources.label: Investigation reports the official toll of 102

events.name: Alexandroupolis–Evros fires
events.summary: The regional outbreak burned near the Turkish border and Dadia forest. Most reported deaths in this tally were migrants found in fire-affected areas; the number is a regional fire-period total, not a count of all people exposed to the fires.

direct.label: 20 reported
direct.detail: Contemporaneous reports attributed 20 deaths to the fires in the region; 18 bodies were found together in the Dadia area.

responders.label: Not separately reported
responders.detail: The linked reports do not identify a confirmed responder fatality count.

sources.label: Regional fire toll reached 20
18 bodies found in the fire-hit forest

events.name: Central-southern Chile fires
events.summary: A heatwave coincided with a large outbreak of fires across central-southern Chile. The early response toll included a firefighter, a helicopter pilot, and a helicopter mechanic.

direct.label: At least 26 reported
direct.detail: A later Reuters report gave a toll of 26 as the fires continued.

responders.label: At least 3 reported
responders.detail: Early AP reporting identified a firefighter, a firefighting helicopter pilot, and a mechanic killed during response operations.

sources.label: Death toll reached at least 24
Updated report: at least 26 deaths
Firefighter and two helicopter crew among early deaths

events.name: Amazon fire season
events.summary: This was a season of many fires across the Amazon biome, not one bounded incident. No single confirmed direct-death total is provided here. A peer-reviewed study estimated additional deaths from fire-related air pollution; those are modeled health impacts, not people documented as dying in the flames.

direct.label: No consolidated direct toll
direct.detail: The linked event coverage does not give a verified direct-fire death total for the full Amazon fire season.

responders.label: Not separately reported
responders.detail: The linked reports do not provide a fire-season total for firefighter or other responder deaths.

smoke.label: ≈3,400 estimated
smoke.detail: A peer-reviewed model estimated additional deaths in 2019 from increased particulate air-pollution exposure associated with the Amazon fires. This is not a direct-fire death count.

sources.label: News report on the Amazon fire surge
Peer-reviewed estimate of smoke-related excess mortality

events.name: Black Summer bushfires
events.summary: A season-long series of fires burned across multiple states. The direct toll is shown separately from estimates of deaths associated with smoke exposure.

direct.label: 33 reported
direct.detail: Direct deaths attributed to the fires in official Australian reporting.

responders.label: 9 reported
responders.detail: Nine firefighters were included in the official direct death toll.

smoke.label: ≈417 estimated
smoke.detail: Public-health research estimated additional deaths associated with smoke exposure; this is not a direct-fire toll.

sources.label: Coverage of the 33 lives lost during Black Summer
Official statement: 33 deaths, including nine firefighters

sources.publisher: Australian Institute of Health and Welfare
sources.label: Public-health analysis of direct and smoke-related deaths

events.name: Camp Fire
events.summary: The Camp Fire destroyed much of Paradise and became California’s deadliest recorded wildfire. The final death count was revised after identification work.

direct.label: 85 reported
direct.detail: Final toll reported by AP and California authorities.

responders.label: Not separately reported
responders.detail: The cited final-toll report does not provide a responder breakdown.

sources.label: Camp Fire killed 85 people

events.name: Mati wildfire
events.summary: A fast-moving fire reached coastal communities east of Athens. The final reported death toll rose after people died from their injuries.

direct.label: 104 reported
direct.detail: Final reported toll for the Mati wildfire.

responders.label: Not separately reported
responders.detail: The cited reports do not provide a verified responder death count.

sources.label: Mati fire killed 104 people

events.name: Tubbs Fire
events.summary: The Tubbs Fire moved through Northern California wine country, including Santa Rosa neighborhoods. It was one of several concurrent fires in the region that month.

direct.label: 22 reported
direct.detail: Deaths attributed specifically to the Tubbs Fire.

responders.label: Not separately reported
responders.detail: The cited report does not state a separate responder death toll for this incident.

sources.label: Report on the fire that killed 22 people

events.name: October Portugal fire outbreak
events.summary: Hundreds of fires spread during extreme wind and dry conditions. This is a separate October outbreak from the June Pedrógão Grande disaster.

direct.label: 50 reported
direct.detail: Portugal’s public broadcaster reported 50 deaths from the October fires.

responders.label: Not separately reported
responders.detail: The cited final-toll report does not give a verified responder death count.

sources.label: Review of the October 2017 fires and 50 deaths

events.name: Pedrógão Grande fire complex
events.summary: A group of fast-moving fires cut through central Portugal. The final official tally included a volunteer firefighter; early news reports carried lower counts while identification continued.

direct.label: 66 reported
direct.detail: Final official toll: 65 civilians and one volunteer firefighter.

responders.label: 1 reported
responders.detail: One volunteer firefighter died from injuries sustained during the response.

sources.label: News coverage of the deadly central Portugal fires
Fire disaster case study and final toll

events.name: Southern Turkey fires
events.summary: Fires burned near southern coastal communities and resorts, prompting evacuations and international firefighting assistance.

direct.label: 8 reported
direct.detail: Reuters reported eight deaths as the fires spread along the southern coast.

responders.label: Not separately reported
responders.detail: The cited tally does not identify responder deaths separately.

sources.label: Death toll rose to eight as fires reached coastal areas

events.name: Kabylia wildfires
events.summary: Multiple fires affected northern Algeria. Soldiers were deployed to help residents and fight the fires; dozens of them died in the response.

direct.label: 90 reported
direct.detail: Reported total for the August 2021 fires.

responders.label: 33 soldiers reported
responders.detail: The IFRC described 33 members of the People's National Army deployed as firefighters among the dead.

sources.label: Coverage of Algeria’s recurring wildfire risk, including the 2021 disaster

sources.publisher: International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies
sources.label: Situation report: 90 deaths, including 33 soldiers fighting fires
